name: Bauhaus Mosque
summary: An oversized half-disc, a thick rectangular minaret, and an open doorway form an asymmetric modernist mosque.
why: The giant cream dome is deliberately shifted to one side. A heavy charcoal minaret and hall balance it without symmetry or ornament. Vermilion, cream, and charcoal give the mosque the directness of a graphic poster.
risk: The geometric reduction can first read as abstract architecture. The off-center dome, minaret, and pointed doorway supply the mosque cues when seen together.
key2: The heavy tower and open doorway
sub2: Clear architecture with almost no detail
reasonToChoose: You want an instantly graphic mosque with the character of a modernist poster.
